Smashed windows have yet to be replaced; the walls are still black with soot from fires that broke out during the protests. Albaniahas seen nearly five months of peaceful anti-government protests, sparked initially when plans were made public that Jared Kushner — a son-in-law ofUS President Donald Trump— and associates intended to build a luxury hotel complex within a nature reserve. Since then, anti-government and anti-corruption protests have escalated. Now, college and high school students clash with police forces almost daily, with the fiercest clashes so far occurring last week. Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for governor of the US state of Ohio, has called an attack ad against her that features her estranged mother "despicable". Acton commented on the campaign ad from her Republican opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy, on Wednesday, saying: "This is despicable, what he's done". In the ad Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, says Acton "lied her entire life". But it does not mention that Arthur's husband was charged with raping Acton when she was a child and that Acton and her brother were then removed from Arthur's custody. The ad set off a storm of criticism from members of both parties. On Thursday, President Donald Trump sought to defend it and Ramaswamy on social media. Acton and Ramaswamy are both running to replace outgoing Governor Mike DeWine, a Republican who endorsed Ramaswamy, in the 3 November midterm election. In a sign that Ramaswamy may have hurt his chances at winning, DeWine has reportedly described the ad as deeply troubling and called for it to be taken down. "I've never attacked his family. I would never do that," Acton said about Ramaswamy at the campaign stop on Wednesday evening. "You can see that there are so many people who have experienced trauma and abuse in their lives," she continued, referring to the fallout from the ad. The last time Acton saw her mother was in a courtroom in 1978 after her stepfather was indicted, according to Acton's campaign. India has strongly rejected references to the country in a report by a United Nations expert on migrants’ human rights, calling them “imprecise and unsupported” and arguing that country-specific allegations must be backed by verifiable evidence and accurate geographical references. Barkha Tamrakar, Deputy Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), raised the objections during an interactive dialogue with Gehad Madi, the UN Special Rapporteur on the Human Rights of Migrants. She criticised inaccuracies in the report and questioned its treatment of legal provisions, evidence and state responsibility. “India must place on record a serious concern about the report’s treatment of law, evidence, and state responsibility. A thematic report must not convert broad policy preferences, unverified allegations, or advocacy submissions into settled findings of the UN,” Tamrakar said. A key objection concerned paragraph 27, footnote 32, which refers to “Assan and Northern India” as an example. Tamrakar said that this is the complete reference and does not identify a case, a proceeding, an authority, a date, a law, or a source. “Assan is not the name of an Indian state or a recognised jurisdiction. headlines.full_text: Why a student protest movement is challenging 12 years of Vučić rule in Serbia After two years of student protests, Serbians vote on Sunday in elections that could bring down the ruling party. Rallies have been taking place across Serbia on Thursday, the final day of campaigning ahead of a snap election billed as a referendum on the country's future. After two years of student protests, Serbians vote for a new parliament on Sunday in elections that threaten populist leader Aleksandar Vučić's 12 years in power. The main threat to Vučić's dominance in Serbian politics comes from a two-year-old student movement, but there are concerns surrounding the fairness of the vote. They have no obvious leaders and are not used to politics, but the "Student List-Students Win" movement has attracted anti-government voters across Serbia. The Student List is fielding candidates from across Serbian society - and as he joined students marching towards Belgrade, lead candidate and cardiologist Ilija Srdanović said history was being rewritten: "The energy is unstoppable." It all began on 1 November 2024, when the concrete canopy collapsed outside Novi Sad train station, in Serbia's second biggest city, killing 16 people. The tragedy was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence in Serbia. Critics linked the station's fatally flawed renovation to a president who had closely associated himself with the project. What started as weekly student protests demanding justice on university campuses and city streets soon became a national movement, often at a local level, that encompassed far more sections of Serbian society, including farmers, actors and judges. Waving “students are winning” flags and blowing whistles, the marchers converged on Slavija Square, the site of some of the movement’s biggest protests. The vote follows nearly two years of student-led protests triggered by the 2024 collapse of a canopy at a newly renovated railway station in Novi Sad that killed 16 people. headlines.full_text: Paris extends curfew as Marseille and Lyon ban protests after riots Protests will only be allowed in some towns and cities if organised by unions, and top museums will be closed on Saturday. Paris is extending a partial curfew restricting movement in parts of the city until Monday, as Marseille and Lyon impose a total ban on protests this weekend. The Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums in the French capital will also be closed on Saturday as more demonstrations are expected. France is still reeling from major disorder at the weekend, when large protests against the high cost of living and school conditions were overshadowed by riots and looting that saw business and historic buildings destroyed. In other parts of the country where protests have not been banned completely, only authorised union demonstrations will be allowed on Saturday, President Emmanuel Macron said. Interior Minister Jean-Didier Berger said police deployments would be increased by 20% compared to last weekend, after the government was accused of being blindsided by the scale of the unrest. France's justice minister said on Thursday that 217 people had been jailed over last weekend's disorder after being convicted in fast-track trials, with that number expected to rise. Gérald Darmanin said 2,700 people had been arrested across France and more than 1,000 have appeared in court. Half of those detained had no prior criminal record, he said, according to Le Figaro newspaper. Police in Paris said its curfew in Place de la République, where protesters gathered last weekend, and the Les Halles shopping area will be extended until Monday. headlines.full_text: Curfew imposed in two districts of Paris until October 25 Both adults and minors are prohibited from visiting the Place de la Republique area and the Les Halles quarter PARIS, October 22. /TASS/. The Paris Police Prefecture has imposed a curfew until October 25 on two districts of the French capital, the authority said in a post on the X social network. "The Paris Police Prefect has issued an order imposing a curfew prohibiting both adults and minors from being present in the Place de la Republique area and the Les Halles quarter daily from 11:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. the following day between October 22 and 25," the statement says. Earlier, the prefecture of the Bouches-du-Rhone department announced a curfew in Marseille for the upcoming weekend. Mass rallies against rising fuel prices and declining purchasing power took place across France, including in the capital, Paris, on October 17. According to organizers, 800,000 people took part in the demonstrations, while the Interior Ministry put the figure at 550,000. In several cities, protests escalated into riots and clashes with police. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez pledged that all those involved in vandalism and looting would be held accountable.

Putin, interviewed on Russian television a day after meeting US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff, confirmed that Russia was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month. He restated longstanding Kremlin policy that Russia never wanted to launch a war, but had run into hostile reactions from Ukraine on key issues of concern to Moscow. Talks on a variety of matters could lead to a positive outcome, he said, but Russia remained intent on a solution ending the conflict rather than a short-lived ceasefire. "The goal of these talks will be to ensure the security of Ukraine and Russia after reaching peace agreements, in their final form, not as a result of a temporary ceasefire for some short period of time. We are ready to resume these contacts to achieve this goal," Putin said. The Russian president said Witkoff also stressed that discussions had to extend to "the architecture of European security as a whole. And I agree with that too. Well, let's see how things develop in the coming days." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who met Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday, said Ukraine was ready for talks likely to take place by early next month. headlines.full_text: Lula says rival should be disqualified over alleged Meta interference ahead of Brazil vote The Brazilian president accuses the tech firm of favouring Flávio Bolsonaro, which it denies. Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's campaign has requested the disqualification of right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaroin the lead up to the final round of the presidential electionon Sunday over alleged interference by social media company Meta. In a petition filed to the country's top electoral court on Wednesday, the leftist incumbent president accused Meta, the tech giant behind Whatsapp, Instagram and Facebook, of limiting its content to boost Bolsonaro's campaign. In response, Bolsonaro filed a petition seeking to disqualify Lula over what he said was the mass dissemination of government posts on WhatsApp. The company has denied the campaigns have been treated unequally. It comes after UN experts said on Wednesday that they were concerned about reports of discrepancies in the ability of each campaign to reach voters on Meta's platforms. A report led by the UN's special rapporteur on freedom of expression said Meta must ensure a level playing field online during the election. It cited incidents including "temporary interruptions of one candidate's campaign account; differences in audience engagement, user feeds, view counts and reach; restrictions on that campaign's Instagram posts". "Information, including from Meta employees, suggests that accounts linked to one side of the presidential race were disproportionately curtailed," it read. Brazil picks its path: What’s at stake in the election Brazilian President Lula is facing off against Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff election with consequences for the entire BRICS group
Read Full Article at RT.com Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is once again fighting for his political future, in a runoff election against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro. After a dirty campaign, voters will decide on Sunday whether Brazil maintains its leftward trajectory or lurches to the right. Bolsonaro defeated Lula in the first round of this year’s presidential election, beating the incumbent left-winger by 47.03% to 45.16% on October 5. With neither candidate winning an outright majority, ten runners-up were eliminated and a runoff called for October 25. Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, more commonly referred to as ‘Lula’, has been a mainstay in Brazilian politics since the 1980s. After serving two terms as president from 2003 to 2011, he was sentenced to nine years in prison in 2017 for alleged involvement in a corruption and money laundering scheme within the state-run oil company Petrobras. Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court struck down his conviction in 2021, and Lula returned to politics the following year, defeating Jair Bolsonaro by a margin of just 0.11%. "We didn't find cars or transportation. One kind person brought us here [on the fourth day] while others refused." As the family walked, the twins got weaker, according to their mother Lina. "They were exhausted… there was cold and dust. Their vomiting and diarrhoea got worse." His ministers praised what did not exist, and the public followed, until a child finally cried out: “But he hasn't got anything on!” TEHRAN - In 1837, Danish author Hans Christian Andersen published The Emperor’s New Clothes, the story of a vain ruler deceived into believing he was wearing magnificent garments invisible to fools and those unfit for office. His ministers praised what did not exist, and the public followed, until a child finally cried out: “But he hasn't got anything on!” Nearly two centuries later, Washington appears to be staging its own version of Andersen’s famous procession. Donald Trump continues to parade American power before the world, surrounded by officials applauding his decisions, even as the economic, military and political consequences of his confrontation with Iran expose a far less flattering reality. Andersen’s emperor was not ruined by deception alone, but by the cowardice of those who knew the truth and chose to protect his pride. Washington’s problem today looks remarkably similar. That child’s voice is the only honest sound in West Asia today. It rises from the ruins of Gaza, from the bombed suburbs of Beirut, from the defiant streets of Tehran, screams from the Minab school, from the mountains of Yemen. It says what the courtiers of Washington and Tel Aviv dare not: the American empire is naked. Its clothes are the fiction of victory. Its tailors are the lobbyists and generals who stitch wars from other people’s children. And the emperor, draped in the tattered myth of moral authority, continues his procession while his own people shiver. Look at the latest spectacle.

headlines.full_text: Ukrainian conflict can only be resolved through talks, US ready to act as mediator — Rubio The US Secretary of State stressed that it is a very difficult conflict to end NEW DELHI, October 22. /TASS/. The current conflict in Ukraine can only be resolved at the negotiating table and the US is ready for a mediation role, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in an interview with theIndia TodayTV channel. "It’s a very difficult conflict to end," he said, noting that US President Donald Trump is paying a great deal of attention to it. "We have people who do nothing all day but trying to find a way to make a difference and to bridge those differences or ways to overcome the existing disagreements." "It’s been difficult, but I can tell you this: hard as it is, it is impossible to do unless both sides are at the table talking and we are happy to play the mediating role in that regard. That’s what we are trying to do. I am not claiming that getting them in the same room is going to solve the problem, but we have no chance to solve it, if we can’t get them in a room," Rubio said. "The question is whether there is some accommodation where both sides will have to make some concessions in order to bring an end to the war. This war is not going to be solved militarily, this war is only going to end diplomatically. The question is: can you arrive at an outcome, in which both sides receive something, a benefit, but also give concessions and bring this to an end," the secretary of state declared. Earlier, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that Russia highly values the US mediation efforts to resolve the conflict in Ukraine.

headlines.full_text: Zaporozhye NPP receives 10-year operating license for power unit No. 6 This marks another stage in ZNPP systematic efforts to obtain the necessary permits in accordance with Russian nuclear energy regulations MELITOPOL, October 22. /TASS/. The Zaporozhye Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) has received a 10-year operating license for power unit No. 6 from Russia’s Federal Environmental, Industrial, and Nuclear Supervision Service (Rostekhnadzor), valid until October 21, 2036. This establishes a legal framework for the plant’s continued safe operation, the NPP said. "The Zaporozhye NPP has received an operating license for power unit No. 6 from Rostekhnadzor. The license was issued for 10 years, until October 21, 2036. <…> Licensing establishes a legal framework for the plant’s continued safe operation. However, obtaining the license does not in itself mean that electricity generation will resume. Any change in the power unit’s operating mode will require a separate decision and compliance with all necessary safety requirements," the plant said on its Max channel. The plant noted that this marks another stage in its systematic efforts to obtain the necessary permits in accordance with Russian nuclear energy regulations. Power unit No. 6 is the third unit at the Zaporozhye NPP to receive a Russian operating license. Rostekhnadzor previously issued licenses for power unit No. 1 in December 2025 and power unit No. 2 in February 2026. The plant has also obtained licenses to operate radiation sources and its dry spent nuclear fuel storage facility.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece simply reports the issuance of a 10‑year operating license without evaluative language.

If yours is among them, here are some last-minute tax-filing tips to keep in mind as the Tuesday, April 18 deadline approaches. Not everyone has to file on April 18:If you live in a federally declared disaster area, have a business there — or have relevant tax documents stored by businesses in that area — it’s likely the IRS has already extended the filing and payment deadlines for you.Hereis where you can find the specific extension dates for each disaster area. Thanks to many rounds of extreme weather in recent months, for instance, tax filers in most of California — which accounts for 10% to 15% of all federal filers — have already been granted an extension until Oct. 16 to file and to pay, according to an IRS spokesperson. If you’re in the armed forces and are currently or were recently stationed in a combat zone, the filing and payment deadlines for your 2022 taxes are most likely extended by 180 days. But your specific extended filing and payment deadlines will depend on the day you leave (or left) the combat zone.This IRS publicationoffers more detail. Taxes and adulting: What to know about filing taxes on your own for the first time Lastly, if you made little to no money last year (typically less than $12,950 for single filers and $25,900 for married couples), you may not be required to file a return.

Spending at US retailers fell in March as consumers pulled back after the banking crisis fueled recession fears. Retail sales, which are adjusted for seasonality but not for inflation, fell by 1% in March from the prior month, the Commerce Department reported on Friday. That was steeper than an expected 0.4% decline, according to Refinitiv, and above the revised 0.2% decline in the prior month. Investors chalk up some of the weakness to a lack of tax returns and concerns about a slowing labor market. The IRS issued $84 billion in tax refunds this March, about $25 billion less than they issued in March of 2022, according to BofA analysts. That led consumers to pull back in spending at department stores and on durable goods, such as appliances and furniture. Spending at general merchandise stores fell 3% in March from the prior month and spending at gas stations declined 5.5% during the same period. Excluding gas station sales, retail spending retreated 0.6% in March from February. However, retail spending rose 2.9% year-over-year. Smaller tax returns likely played a role in last month’s decline in retail sales, along with the expiration of enhanced food assistance benefits, economists say. “March is a really important month for refunds. Lake Powell, the second-largest human-made reservoir in the US, has lost nearly 7% of its potential storage capacity since 1963, when Glen Canyon Dam was built, a new report shows. In addition to water loss due to anintense multiyear drought, the US Geological Survey and the Bureau of Reclamationreport found, Lake Powell faced an average annual loss in storage capacity of about 33,270 acre-feet, or 11 billion gallons, per year between 1963 and 2018. That’s enough water to fill the Reflecting Pool on the National Mall about 1,600 times. The capacity of the reservoir is shrinking because of sediments flowing in from theColorado and San Juan rivers, according to the report. Those sediments settle at the bottom of the reservoir and decrease the total amount of water the reservoir can hold. As of Monday, Lake Powell was around 25% full, according to data from the Bureau of Reclamation. It’s bad news for a region already facing water shortages and extreme wildfires due to the drought. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration drought experts said last week these conditions areexpected to at least continue– if not worsen – in the coming months. Lake Powell is an important reservoir in the Colorado River Basin. Both Lake Powell and nearby Lake Mead, the nation’s largest reservoir, have drained at an alarming rate. headlines.full_text: Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787 Overruns Munich Runway During Takeoff, Returns Safely A Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on a Munich-Hanoi flight returned to Munich after a serious incident during takeoff. The aircraft overran the runway, suffered a tailstrike, and experienced tyre damage. Passengers evacuated safely. A Vietnam Airlines Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner operating a Munich-Hanoi flight returned to Munich Airport on Saturday after reportedly suffering a serious incident during takeoff, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24 and the airline. Flight VN-34, operated by Boeing 787-9 aircraft VN-A867, reportedly rotated extremely late during takeoff and overran the runway before becoming airborne. Preliminary reports said the aircraft travelled around 120 metres beyond the runway end, entering the grass and coming close to the first row of approach lights. The aircraft also reportedly suffered a tailstrike and tyre damage. After takeoff, the aircraft climbed to around 10,000 feet before the crew received a tyre-pressure indication and decided to dump fuel before returning to Munich. Flightradar24 said the aircraft circled for more than two hours to burn fuel. Around 90 minutes after departure, the Boeing 787 made two low approaches to Munich's Runway 26R before landing safely. Smoke was reportedly seen coming from the left main landing gear, after which the aircraft became disabled on the runway. Passengers were evacuated using emergency slides, with the fire brigade present at the scene, according to Flightradar24. Vietnam Airlines said the Hanoi-bound flight returned to its departure airport due to a "technical issue", without providing further details. "The flight crew followed all required procedures and landed safely at Munich Airport. The passengers and cabin crew members

headlines.full_text: Russia’s Khachanov advances to quarterfinals at 2026 Almaty Open tennis tournament Karen Khachanov is now set to play in the quarterfinals round against Alexander Bublik from Kazakhstan ALMATY, October 22. /TASS/. Russia’s Karen Khachanov has advanced to the quarterfinals stage at the 2026 Almaty Open tennis tournament after defeating Tomas Machac from the Czech Republic on Thursday. The 5th-seeded Russian, who is playing under a neutral status at the tournament, outplayed his Czech opponent 6-2; 4-6; 7-6 (9-7). Hitting his spots, playing even more powerful, more precise… I had to really stay there until the end," Khachanov added. A seven-time ATP champion, Khachanov, 30, is currently the 25th-ranked player in the world. His best performance in the Grand Slam series was when he reached the semifinal rounds at the 2022, 2026 US Open and the 2023 Australian Open. The Russian player also took home the silver medal in men’s singles at the 2020 Summer Olympic Games in Tokyo. He also won the 2021 Davis Cup as part of the Russian national team. The 2026 Almaty Open is the ATP 250 class tournament played on indoor hardcourts on October 19-25 and it offers $1.075 million in prize money. Mark Carney is pursuing new trade agreements and strategic partnerships as US tariffs expose the risks of relying on one market Mark Carney is pursuing new trade agreements and strategic partnerships as US tariffs expose the risks of relying on one market Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's visit to Turkey on Thursday is the latest step in a broader effort to diversify the country's trade relationships, expand export markets and strengthen economic resilience amid tensions with the United States. From a trade deal with China to negotiations for a comprehensive economic agreement with India and closer cooperation with Turkey, Ottawa is seeking new opportunities for Canadian businesses in energy, agriculture, defence, technology and critical minerals. The push comes as US President Donald Trump's tariffs disrupt established trade relationships and raise concerns about jobs and investment in Canadian industries. Yet the government insists that diversification is not about abandoning the US market. Speaking at the Toronto Global Forum on Wednesday, International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu said the strategy was intended to give Canadian businesses more options rather than replace their largest trading partner. Carney travelled to Beijing in January to reset strained relations with China, securing an agreement that reduced tariffs on Canadian canola and Chinese electric vehicles. China offers a substantial market for Canadian agricultural products and other exports. headlines.full_text: Brent crude oil hits highest since May as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia fuel global oil supply fears Brent crude hits its highest level since May as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, Strait of Hormuz tensions and oil supply disruptions fuel market fears. Brent crude oil prices rose to their highest level since May on Thursday after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group carried out more attacks in Saudi Arabia. The attacks raised fears that the conflict in the Middle East could spread further and disrupt oil supplies from one of the world's most important oil-exporting regions. Brent crude futures rose by $3.35, or 3.08%, to $112.17 a barrel by 0818 GMT on Thursday. This was the highest level since May 18. Brent prices had touched $112.55 a barrel earlier in the trading session. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also moved higher. WTI crude rose by $2.68, or 2.76%, to $99.83 a barrel, according to Reuters. Oil market analysts said efforts to reduce tensions in Ukraine and the Middle East were not convincing enough to calm the markets. Attacks on ships in theStrait of Hormuzand Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and its oil infrastructure were raising concerns about oil supplies, despite reports that Middle Eastern crude exports had recovered to levels above those seen before the conflict, PVM Oil analyst Tamas Varga said. Varga also said he did not expect the conflicts to ease before the US midterm elections. He said this could keep oil prices high in the coming weeks, according to Reuters. Despite the security concerns, Middle Eastern crude oil exports remained high. headlines.full_text: Pope Leo welcomed back as he delivers Angelus prayer days after lung cancer surgery Thousands gathered in St. Peter's Square as Pope Leo XIV made a surprise early return from Gemelli hospital following cancerous tumor removal. A crowd of supporters greet Pope Leo XIV outside of Gemelli Hospital in Rome, Italy, on Saturday, Oct. 17 as the pontiff returns to the Vatican following surgery to remove a cancerous node in his right lung. Credit: Reuters. Pope Leo XIVmade a remarkable return to the Vatican on Sunday, appearing before thousands of Catholic faithful in St. Peter's Square just five days after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his lung. The 71-year-old pontiff delivered his traditional Angelus prayer from a window overlooking the square, marking his first official engagement since being discharged Saturday fromRome's Gemelli hospital, where doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung. Leo thanked the faithful for their prayers and support throughout his hospitalization, saying his recent health struggles had brought him closer to those suffering from illness. He also expressed gratitude to the doctors, nurses and hospital staff who cared for him following the operation. headlines.full_text: Pakistan's Supreme Court Orders Former PM Imran Khan to Be Moved to Hospital from Jail Amid Health Concerns The Supreme Court of Pakistan ordered former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be moved to a hospital from jail due to health concerns. He has been imprisoned since August 2023 and faces multiple cases following his ousting in 2022. Islamabad:The Supreme Court of Pakistan ordered on Tuesday that former Prime Minister Imran Khan ​be moved to a hospital from jail, his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party ‌said, meeting a longstanding demand of his party and family, who had raised concerns about his health. Cricketer-turned-politician Khan, 73, has been in jail since August ​2023, convicted in a string of cases that he ​says were politically driven following his ouster in 2022. A three-member Supreme Court bench, headed by Justice Shahid Wahid and comprising Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, issued the ruling on Imran's petition for his hospitalisation. His sons ⁠repeatedly expressed concern regarding his deteriorating health last year, with his ​lawyers saying he had lost significant vision in his right eye ​while in prison. "It's a very welcome order, and we wish it had happened sooner so his eye and general health would not have deteriorated this much," ​PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari said. "He should remain in hospital until all ​doctors are satisfied," he said. The court has directed Khan be moved to Shifa ‌International ⁠Hospital within 48 hours and remain there until September 16, Khan's spokesperson Naeem Haider Panjutha said on X. Since he lost power in a no-confidence vote, Khan has faced multiple cases, including over state ​gifts and an ​unlawful marriage. headlines.full_text: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs as AI-led cost-cutting drive expands after mixed Q3 results and trading revenue falls Barclays plans to cut 5,000 jobs as it expands AI-led cost savings, after reporting mixed third-quarter results and a 19% fall in fixed-income trading revenue. British bank Barclays Plc has announced plans to cut 5,000 jobs, or about 5% of its total workforce, as part of a wider effort to reduce costs and improve efficiency using technology and artificial intelligence (AI). According to Barclays' third-quarter earnings statement, the bank is focusing on simplifying its organisation and making its operations more efficient. About 60% of the planned job cuts will affect support functions, including developers. Barclays had already cut around 1,000 jobs during the first six months of 2026. The remaining cuts are expected to take place before the end of the year. According to Bloomberg, Barclays employed around 93,000 people globally at the end of 2025. Barclays Chief Executive Officer CS Venkatakrishnan said the bank plans to use AI on a large scale but stressed that the technology is only one part of its cost-cutting strategy. “We will employ AI at scale,” he said. “But AI is the icing on the cake, not the cake.” Venkatakrishnan made these remarks during a call with reporters, according to Bloomberg. The announcement came as Barclays reported its third-quarter earnings on Thursday. The bank's results missed several analyst estimates, with weakness in its investment banking business offsetting stronger performance in some other areas. The bank's bond traders recorded a particularly sharp decline in performance during the quarter, while its equities trading business delivered strong growth.
